client’s potassium, magnesium, and vitamin B12 levels. 
2 . a. The health care provider would be expected to check the client’s iron level. Iron deficiency can cause

vitamin B12, iron, and magnesium levels.

5 . d. With Crohn’s disease, and when a client has many bowel movements daily, absorption becomes a problem. 
In particular, iron, calcium, and vitamin D are not absorbed properly in this disease process. 
6 . c. The nurse should expect supplementation to be ordered. Enteral supplementation will likely be used, but if 
that is not sufficient, parenteral supplementation may be considered.
